title: Steering vs. self-preference: replicating activation-based debiasing of an LLM evaluator

original_idea.body: Set up a self-preferring open LLM-judge, build a self-preference CAA vector, steer it out, and measure the bias/accuracy tradeoff.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Unbiased LLM-judge infra is foundational but the chain to catastrophic-risk reduction is moderate/indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Set up a judge, build a self-preference vector, steer + measure tradeoff; guided, novice + mentor feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable but requires constructing a self-preference setup plus bias/accuracy measurement.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open-source LLM-judge debiasing is foundational, lab-deprioritized infra; public model, no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + cheap vector on a small model; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: The activation-debias-of-self-preference method is published; replication/stress-test on small open judges is partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The self-preference steering fix is published; replicating and stress-testing it on small open judges is a partly-open extension.
